findings.title: Google still received data after you rejected cookies
findings.detail: 5 requests to googletagmanager.com after you clicked reject (Advertising).
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device)

findings.severity_note: Lowered from high: no substantial advertising or session-replay evidence cited (a tracking cookie, activity after reject, or 3+ requests to an actual tracking domain; a tag loader like Google Tag Manager alone doesn't count), so an exemption or innocent explanation is plausible.
findings.title: Advertising-related Google activity conflicted with the cookie policy
findings.detail: After the reject option was successfully selected, the audit recorded five requests to Google Tag Manager classified as advertising activity. Croda's cookie policy says consent is required for non-essential cookies, including advertising cookies.
findings.policy_quote: Your consent is required for the use of cookies, but not for the use of cookies that are essential in order to provide the website.
findings.reasoning: The recorded post-rejection advertising activity is inconsistent with the policy's consent requirement and creates a direct transparency and fairness problem. The severity is high because the evidence concerns advertising-related activity continuing after the user rejected non-essential cookies; the underlying request contents were not available, so this finding is limited to the recorded classification and policy contradiction.
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EU GDPR Art. 5(1)(a)

letter.subject: Concern regarding cookie and tracking activity after rejection on croda.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns about cookie and tracking activity observed on https://croda.com during an automated, passive audit on 2026-11-08 04:11 UTC. The audit used a fresh browser, clicked the cookie banner’s reject option (“ACCEPT ONLY ESSENTIAL COOKIES”), and then recorded what was still sent while browsing the site.

The pages visited after rejection were:
1. https://www.croda.com/ja-jp
2. https://www.croda.com/en-gb/our-markets
3. https://www.croda.com/en-gb/our-markets/consumer-care

I also reviewed your privacy policy at:
1. https://www.croda.com/en-gb/privacy-policy

Please could you explain the following points:
1. After the reject option was selected, Google still received data. The audit observed 5 requests to googletagmanager.com after rejection. This was classified as advertising-related activity.
2. Our automated review suggests this advertising-related Google activity appears to conflict with your cookie policy. After the reject option was successfully selected, the audit recorded five requests to Google Tag Manager classified as advertising activity. Your cookie policy states: “Your consent is required for the use of cookies, but not for the use of cookies that are essential in order to provide the website.”

In light of the above, please:
1. Explain each of the points set out above.
2. Confirm which cookies, trackers or related requests you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking or similar activity from occurring without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

I would also be grateful if you could clarify how the observed requests to googletagmanager.com operate when a user has selected the reject option, and on what basis you consider that activity compatible with your current cookie settings and published policy.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
findings_used: Google still received data after you rejected cookies
Advertising-related Google activity conflicted with the cookie policy

ai_review.summary: The audit found advertising-related Google Tag Manager requests continuing after the cookie banner's reject option was successfully selected. This appears inconsistent with Croda's stated requirement for consent for non-essential cookies and raises concerns under PECR reg. 6 and UK GDPR transparency and fairness requirements. The policy otherwise covers many UK GDPR information topics, although retention is described by a general criterion rather than a specific period.
evidence: E1: Cookie banner found: True. Reject clicked successfully: True. Method: llm. Buttons clicked: ACCEPT ONLY ESSENTIAL COOKIES.

E2: Tracker Google (Advertising): 1 requests before consent, 5 after reject, to googletagmanager.com. Example after-reject requests: https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-KJ8QF92 | https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-KJ8QF92
E3: Pages browsed and scrolled after reject: https://www.croda.com/ja-jp, https://www.croda.com/en-gb/our-markets, https://www.croda.com/en-gb/our-markets/consumer-care.

E4: Privacy policy: https://www.croda.com/en-gb/privacy-policy. Companies it names: Webeo, Lead Forensics, Mailchimp, ON24, Adobe, Sitecore, Email Labs, Jotform, Sleeknote, SnapEngage, Survey Monkey, Doodle Survey, Google, Investis. Contact email found: dataprotection.GB@croda.com.
E6: Automated check (high): Google still received data after you rejected cookies. 5 requests to googletagmanager.com after you clicked reject (Advertising).
